core_obligations: The description and exactness (proof lines 5223-5237): the lower adjoint is the sheafification of the left Kan extension, which is the direct image along the left adjoint; right exactness comes from adjunction, and left exactness from the commutation of the direct image with finite limits together with exactness of sheafification.
A continuous left adjoint (proof lines 5240-5242): in that case the sheafification is unnecessary and the induced functor on sheaves provides the left adjoint.
A cocontinuous left adjoint (proof lines 5245-5248): the first equality follows from the description and the definitions, and the second from uniqueness of adjoints, with an alternative route named.
proof_roadmap: Identify the lower adjoint with a sheafification and compute its exactness.
Treat the case of a continuous left adjoint using the induced functor on sheaves.
Treat the case of a cocontinuous left adjoint using uniqueness of adjoints.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects consequences of a left adjoint existing for a cocontinuous and continuous functor: the lower adjoint is the sheafification of the direct image along the left adjoint and is exact, a continuous left adjoint gives a left adjoint for the lower adjoint, and a cocontinuous left adjoint identifies the two morphisms of topoi up to the expected interchange (statement lines 5199-5220). The proof is a complete argument: the description follows from the identification of the left Kan extension with the direct image along the left adjoint, and exactness is assembled from adjunction, commutation with finite limits and exactness of sheafification (proof lines 5223-5237); the continuous case uses the induced functor on sheaves (proof lines 5240-5242); and the cocontinuous case follows from the description and uniqueness of adjoints (proof lines 5245-5248). The non-formal content is the exactness assembly and the two special cases. The claim is H2: several steps, each with its input named.
